newsitem.title: USA: Conoco's Petrozuata venture awards pipe contracts.
newsitem.headline: Conoco's Petrozuata venture awards pipe contracts.

text.p: Conoco Inc said Petrozuata, its joint with Maraven, has awarded four pipe supply contracts.

The DuPont Co subsidiary said contracts worth $44.9 were awarded to two Venezuelan firms -- Industria Mecanics Orion SA and Soldadura y Tuberiss de Oriente CA -- to supply 36-inch pipe for a new crude oil pipeline to be constructed in Venezuela.

The 125-mile, (200 kilometer), 36-inch pipeline will transport extra-heavy crude from the venture's 55,000 acre field in the Zuata region of Venezuela's Orinoco belt to a facility at the Jose Industrial Complex on the northern coast.
Pipeline construction will begin this year and will be completed in 1998, Conoco said.
A third Venezuelan firm, Atlantida Internacional CS, will coat the pipe at their pipe coating facility in Venezuela as part of the pipe supply contract.

Another $16.6 million contract was awarded to Confab Industrial SA for the supply of pipe for another 20-inch, 125-mile pipeline which will be used to return a diluent stream to the field. Diluent will be mixed with the heavy oil in order to transport it to Jose. Afterwards, the diluent will be extracted, returned to the field and reused.
